decisions.decision: What does the fish value login_shell hold?
decisions.ruling: The path of the login shell, default /opt/homebrew/bin/fish in [defaults]. [mise.bootstrap.user] login_shell = "<% index .config `login_shell` | required `fish: set login_shell in [tools.fish] of macos.toml` %>". A user who wants another login shell writes its path in [tools.fish]. The old bool and its conditional section go.
decisions.rejected: Keep a bool: a [mise.*] table cannot be conditional.

decisions.decision: How does a <% %> expression sit inside a [mise.*] string?
decisions.ruling: The expression sits inside a TOML basic string ("..."), and each string literal inside it is a Go raw string in backticks, never a double quote, so the TOML string needs no escape. The engine renders a tools.toml that holds <% before it generates (P08 D6), so the generated mise file holds the rendered value.
decisions.rejected: Double quotes with TOML escapes inside the action; a TOML literal string.

decisions.decision: Where does the dock_orientation check go?
decisions.ruling: Inside the <% %> expression of [mise.bootstrap.macos.defaults."com.apple.dock"] orientation: required with the message `macos-defaults: set dock_orientation in [tools.macos-defaults] of macos.toml`, then test.Fail when the value is not bottom, left or right, then the value. Each other domain of the old [defaults.domains] becomes [mise.bootstrap.macos.defaults."<domain>"] with the same keys.
decisions.rejected: A separate check file or an engine rule for one value.

decisions.decision: How does the import change a shipped file?
decisions.ruling: Each shipped file keeps its content byte for byte. Only the old header line becomes the new two-line header, and each required message that named <tool>.toml now names [tools.<tool>] of macos.toml. Each old .config/mise/conf.d/* fragment is not shipped: its tables move into [mise.*] of tools.toml.
decisions.rejected: Fix or reformat content during the import; the phase 4 comparison judges each difference.

decisions.decision: What happens to an empty [defaults] table?
decisions.ruling: It goes. A tools.toml has [defaults] only when it holds a value.

decisions.decision: Which header does the gh merge source carry?
decisions.ruling: Its first line `# Merged by macos-setup: tools/gh/.config/gh/config.yml.tmpl` becomes `# Merged by bootstrap: macos/tools/gh/.config/gh/config.yml.tmpl`. It gets no sync header, because a merge target carries no header and the engine does not read this line.
decisions.rejected: The two-line sync header on a merge source.

decisions.decision: Does the plan add test cases?
decisions.ruling: No. test:macos-tools (P10) now meets the init stage (bash, zsh, fish), so its case 1 expects exit 4, then 0. U2 adds the answers of the questions of git, ssh, gh and macos-defaults to the example, from MS/tests/setup-sync/sample-config/.
decisions.rejected: A test case for each tool.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 lands the shell rc files, the ips:* task scripts and mise config that writes /etc/shells, the login shell and the macOS defaults on each Mac. One review unit in wave 2 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit: the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Can this plan run in parallel with another plan of the chain?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Does the plan run setup:configs or the Mac sync?
decisions.ruling: No. mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in consumers, and the first Mac run, stay hand steps (Out of scope).
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step that runs them.

decisions.decision: How do the fish seeds move?
decisions.ruling: The three [files] tables with mode = "seed" stay as they are. The three seed files are copied byte for byte with no header, because a seed has no header.
decisions.rejected: Add the sync header to the seeds.

decisions.decision: Which comment edits does the import allow?
decisions.ruling: The exception of P11 D4. A comment that names an old values file of the config folder (gh.toml, git.toml, ssh.toml) now names [tools.<name>] of macos.toml: gh config.yml.tmpl:7, git config.tmpl:3, git identity.tmpl:3 and ssh config.identity.tmpl:3. The unit reports each such edit as DECIDED. No other comment changes (D4).
decisions.rejected: Keep the false comments until the phase 4 comparison.

decisions.decision: Does a security finding in content that this plan imports unchanged from macos-setup stop the run?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05, given at D14 of 2026-11-04-macos-tools-base-core for plans 11 to 14: no. A security finding in content that is byte for byte from macos-setup, apart from the changes that this plan names, is accepted for this import. It does not stop the run, and the content does not change. The run records each such finding as an open gap with its severity and location, for one security plan after the run. A finding in code that this plan writes or changes stops the run as before.
decisions.rejected: Stop on each finding in imported content.

decisions.decision: Does the finding on the mode of ~/.ssh in sync-engine/setup-sync:589 stop this plan (G13, G14)?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05: no. The finding stays open as G13 and G14 for one security plan after the run, and this plan does not change the engine. This ruling covers this finding only. A security review of this plan does not report this case again. Any other finding in engine code stops the run as before.
decisions.rejected: Fix the folder mode in this plan, with a named owner and a test.

[medium] macos/tools/ssh/.ssh/config.tmpl:19 (U1): StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new in Host * takes a first-time host key with no prompt, so an attacker on the path at a first connection can intercept the session and pin a spoofed key. Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run

[medium] macos/tools/zsh/.config/zsh/98-zinit.zsh:8 (U1): lines 8-11 load four third-party plugins with zinit light and no commit pin, so an upstream compromise runs code in every interactive zsh. Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run

[low] macos/tools/fish/.config/fish/conf.d/02-path.fish:30 (U1): fish_add_path puts the user-writable ~/.local/bin ahead of the system folders, unlike bash and zsh. Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run

[low] macos/tools/ssh/.ssh/config.tmpl:22 (U1): AddKeysToAgent yes and UseKeychain yes apply to Host * with no confirm, so code in the user session can sign silently with a key. Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run

[low] macos/tools/git/.config/git/config.tmpl:12 (U1): global core.filemode = false hides executable-bit changes from git status and git diff. Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run

[low] sync-engine/setup-sync:589: when ~/.ssh is missing, the first ssh tool file reaches mkdir -p with no folder mode, so ~/.ssh takes the umask, normally 0755, not 0700. Not reproduced · user ruling D14: open for one security plan after the run; the user approved this record on 2026-11-05

SPEC/PLAN GAP: U1 (01-tools.md, ssh entry) never required ~/.ssh to be mode 0700 when the sync creates it; the requirement belongs in the ssh tool plan or in the folder creation of setup-sync · user ruling D14: open for one security plan after the run

Imported unchanged from macos-setup · D13 applies: content unchanged, open for one security plan after the run
